note: Methods restated in our own words from widely known books on thinking; no text is quoted. Each method is a scaffold, not proof that thinking happened.

stages.frame: Understand and define the problem (request card, MECE, systems map)
stages.diverge: Generate options before judging (ideas, analogies, contradictions)
stages.execute: Build, test and ship in small loops
stages.verify: Audit claims, risks and biases before delivery

books.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
books.author: Daniel Kahneman
books.core_idea_en: Two systems: fast intuition (System 1) produces most judgements and its errors are predictable; slow deliberate reasoning (System 2) is lazy and must be called on purpose.
books.core_idea_ar: نظامان: حدس سريع يصدر أغلب الأحكام وأخطاؤه متوقعة، وتفكير بطيء متأنٍّ كسول لا يعمل إلا إذا استدعيته عمدًا.

books.title: Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment
books.author: Kahneman, Sibony, Sunstein
books.core_idea_en: Besides bias there is noise: unwanted variability between judges and between occasions. Decision hygiene reduces it.
books.core_idea_ar: إلى جانب التحيز توجد الضوضاء: تباين غير مرغوب بين الحكّام وبين المرات. نظافة القرار تقللها.

books.title: The Art of Thinking Clearly
books.author: Rolf Dobelli
books.core_idea_en: A field guide of short, named thinking errors; naming the error at the moment of decision is the defence.
books.core_idea_ar: دليل ميداني لأخطاء تفكير مسماة؛ تسمية الخطأ لحظة القرار هي الوقاية.

books.title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
books.author: Robert Cialdini
books.core_idea_en: Six levers (reciprocity, commitment, social proof, liking, authority, scarcity) move people automatically; know them to use them honestly and to resist them.
books.core_idea_ar: ست روافع تحرك الناس آليًا: المعاملة بالمثل، الالتزام، الدليل الاجتماعي، الإعجاب، السلطة، الندرة؛ اعرفها لتستخدمها بأمانة وتقاومها.

books.title: Superforecasting
books.author: Philip Tetlock & Dan Gardner
books.core_idea_en: Good forecasters break questions down, start from base rates, update in small steps, keep score and stay humble.
books.core_idea_ar: المتنبئون الأفضل يفككون السؤال، يبدأون بالمعدل الأساسي، يحدّثون بخطوات صغيرة، يحتفظون بسجل نتائجهم ويظلون متواضعين.

books.title: Thinking in Bets
books.author: Annie Duke
books.core_idea_en: A decision is a bet under uncertainty; judge decisions by their process and information, not by the single outcome (avoid 'resulting').
books.core_idea_ar: القرار رهان في ظل عدم اليقين؛ احكم على القرار بطريقته ومعلوماته لا بنتيجة واحدة.

books.title: The Black Swan / Antifragile / Fooled by Randomness
books.title_ar: البجعة السوداء وضد الهشاشة والخداع بالعشوائية
books.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
books.core_idea_en: Rare, high-impact events dominate outcomes and cannot be predicted; design for exposure (convex payoffs, redundancy, small bets) rather than for prediction.
books.core_idea_ar: الأحداث النادرة عالية الأثر تهيمن ولا يمكن توقعها؛ صمم للتعرض (مكاسب محدبة، تكرار، رهانات صغيرة) لا للتنبؤ.

books.title: Factfulness
books.author: Hans Rosling
books.core_idea_en: Ten dramatic instincts (gap, negativity, straight line, fear, size, generalization, destiny, single perspective, blame, urgency) distort the world; check with numbers and proportions.
books.core_idea_ar: عشر غرائز درامية تشوّه رؤيتنا للعالم؛ صحح بالأرقام والنسب.

books.title: How to Measure Anything
books.author: Douglas Hubbard
books.core_idea_en: Anything that matters can be measured in the sense of reducing uncertainty; small samples and calibrated ranges are often enough; measure what has the highest information value.
books.core_idea_ar: كل ما يهم يمكن قياسه بمعنى تقليل عدم اليقين؛ العينات الصغيرة والنطاقات المعايرة تكفي غالبًا؛ قِس ما له أعلى قيمة معلوماتية.

books.title: How to Solve It
books.author: George Pólya
books.core_idea_en: Four phases: understand the problem, devise a plan, carry out the plan, look back; with heuristics such as 'solve a simpler related problem' and 'work backwards'.
books.core_idea_ar: أربع مراحل: افهم المسألة، ضع خطة، نفّذها، ثم انظر للخلف؛ مع حيل مثل حل مسألة أبسط مشابهة والعمل من النهاية.

books.title: The 5 Elements of Effective Thinking
books.author: Edward Burger & Michael Starbird
books.core_idea_en: Understand deeply (earth), fail on purpose (fire), raise questions (air), follow the flow of ideas (water), and keep changing (quintessence).
books.core_idea_ar: افهم بعمق، افشل عمدًا لتتعلم، اطرح الأسئلة، تتبع تدفق الأفكار، واستمر في التغير.

books.title: And Suddenly the Inventor Appeared (TRIZ)
books.author: Genrich Altshuller
books.core_idea_en: Inventive problems are contradictions; resolve them with a small set of recurring inventive principles instead of compromise, aiming at the ideal final result.
books.core_idea_ar: مسائل الاختراع تناقضات؛ احلها بمبادئ اختراع متكررة بدل الحل الوسط، مستهدفًا النتيجة المثالية.

books.title: The Pyramid Principle
books.author: Barbara Minto
books.core_idea_en: Start with the answer, then group supporting arguments in MECE sets, each summarising the ideas below it; open with Situation-Complication-Question.
books.core_idea_ar: ابدأ بالإجابة ثم اجمع الحجج الداعمة في مجموعات لا تتداخل وتغطي الكل، وابدأ بالموقف-التعقيد-السؤال.

books.title: Bulletproof Problem Solving
books.author: Charles Conn & Robert McLean
books.core_idea_en: A seven-step loop: define, disaggregate, prioritise, plan work, analyse, synthesise, communicate; iterate with hypotheses.
books.core_idea_ar: حلقة من سبع خطوات: عرّف، فكك، رتب الأولويات، خطط، حلل، اجمع، وصّل؛ مع فرضيات متكررة.

books.title: Conceptual Blockbusting
books.author: James L. Adams
books.core_idea_en: Perceptual, emotional, cultural and intellectual blocks stop ideas; name the block to remove it.
books.core_idea_ar: حواجز إدراكية وعاطفية وثقافية وفكرية تمنع الأفكار؛ سمِّ الحاجز لتزيله.

books.title: Six Thinking Hats
books.author: Edward de Bono
books.core_idea_en: Separate thinking into six modes worn one at a time (facts, feelings, caution, benefits, creativity, process) so a group thinks in parallel instead of arguing.
books.core_idea_ar: افصل التفكير إلى ستة أنماط تُلبس واحدًا تلو الآخر (حقائق، مشاعر، حذر، فوائد، إبداع، إدارة) ليفكر الفريق بالتوازي بدل الجدال.

books.title: Lateral Thinking
books.author: Edward de Bono
books.core_idea_en: Escape dominant patterns by provocation (PO), random entry, challenge and alternatives, separating generation from judgement.
books.core_idea_ar: اهرب من الأنماط السائدة بالاستفزاز والمدخل العشوائي والتحدي والبدائل، وافصل التوليد عن الحكم.

books.title: A Technique for Producing Ideas
books.author: James Webb Young
books.core_idea_en: Ideas are new combinations of old elements; gather specific and general material, digest it, let it incubate, catch the idea, then shape it against reality.
books.core_idea_ar: الأفكار تركيبات جديدة لعناصر قديمة: اجمع، اهضم، احتضن، التقط الفكرة، ثم شكّلها في الواقع.

books.title: Thinkertoys
books.author: Michael Michalko
books.core_idea_en: A toolbox of idea techniques; the best known is SCAMPER: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to other use, Eliminate, Reverse.
books.core_idea_ar: صندوق أدوات للأفكار أشهرها SCAMPER: استبدل، ادمج، كيّف، عدّل، استخدم لغرض آخر، احذف، اعكس.

books.title: Change by Design / Creative Confidence
books.author: Tim Brown; Tom & David Kelley (IDEO)
books.core_idea_en: Design thinking: empathise with people, define the need, ideate widely, prototype cheaply, test with users; diverge then converge (the double diamond).
books.core_idea_ar: التفكير التصميمي: تعاطف مع الناس، عرّف الحاجة، ولّد أفكارًا كثيرة، انمذج بسرعة ورخص، واختبر مع المستخدمين؛ تباعد ثم تقارب.

books.title: Steal Like an Artist
books.author: Austin Kleon
books.core_idea_en: Creativity grows from influences: collect, study the lineage of your heroes, transform and remix rather than copy, and show your work.
books.core_idea_ar: الإبداع ينمو من المؤثرات: اجمع، ادرس سلسلة من تحبهم، حوّل وامزج بدل النسخ، واعرض عملك.

books.title: Thinking in Systems
books.author: Donella Meadows
books.core_idea_en: Behaviour comes from structure: stocks, flows, feedback loops and delays; the leverage points range from parameters (weak) to goals and paradigms (strong).
books.core_idea_ar: السلوك ينتج من البنية: مخزونات وتدفقات وحلقات تغذية راجعة وتأخيرات؛ ونقاط الرافعة من المعاملات (ضعيفة) إلى الأهداف والنماذج الفكرية (قوية).

books.title: The Fifth Discipline
books.author: Peter Senge
books.core_idea_en: Learning organisations practice personal mastery, mental models, shared vision, team learning and systems thinking; recurring problems follow archetypes.
books.core_idea_ar: المنظمات المتعلمة تمارس الإتقان الشخصي والنماذج الذهنية والرؤية المشتركة وتعلم الفريق والتفكير المنظومي؛ والمشكلات المتكررة تتبع أنماطًا.

books.title: Good Strategy Bad Strategy
books.author: Richard Rumelt
books.core_idea_en: A good strategy has a kernel: a diagnosis of the challenge, a guiding policy, and coherent actions; bad strategy is fluff, goals posing as strategy, or failure to face the problem.
books.core_idea_ar: للاستراتيجية الجيدة نواة: تشخيص التحدي، وسياسة موجهة، وأفعال متسقة؛ والسيئة حشو أو أهداف تتنكر كاستراتيجية.

books.title: Sources of Power
books.author: Gary Klein
books.core_idea_en: Experts decide by recognising patterns and mentally simulating one option (recognition-primed decision); the pre-mortem harnesses this to find failure in advance.
books.core_idea_ar: الخبراء يقررون بالتعرف على الأنماط ومحاكاة خيار واحد ذهنيًا؛ وتمرين «ما قبل الوفاة» يستغل ذلك لكشف الفشل مسبقًا.

books.title: The Art of War
books.author: Sun Tzu
books.core_idea_en: Know yourself and the other side, win before the battle by positioning, avoid strength and strike weakness, and adapt like water.
books.core_idea_ar: اعرف نفسك وخصمك، انتصر قبل المعركة بالتموضع، تجنب القوة واضرب الضعف، وتكيّف كالماء.

books.title: Decisive
books.author: Chip & Dan Heath
books.core_idea_en: WRAP: Widen your options, Reality-test your assumptions, Attain distance before deciding, Prepare to be wrong.
books.core_idea_ar: WRAP: وسّع الخيارات، اختبر الافتراضات بالواقع، ابتعد قبل القرار، واستعد للخطأ.

books.title: The Lean Startup
books.author: Eric Ries
books.core_idea_en: Build-measure-learn loops with a minimum viable product, actionable metrics and explicit pivot-or-persevere decisions.
books.core_idea_ar: حلقات بناء-قياس-تعلم بأقل منتج قابل للتجربة، ومقاييس قابلة للفعل، وقرار صريح بالتحول أو المثابرة.

books.title: The Great Mental Models
books.author: Shane Parrish (Farnam Street)
books.core_idea_en: A latticework of models from many disciplines: map is not territory, circle of competence, first principles, thought experiment, second-order thinking, probabilistic thinking, inversion, Occam's and Hanlon's razors.
books.core_idea_ar: شبكة نماذج من تخصصات كثيرة: الخريطة ليست الأرض، دائرة الكفاءة، المبادئ الأولى، التجربة الذهنية، التفكير من الدرجة الثانية، الاحتمالات، القلب، شفرة أوكام وهانلون.

books.title: The Scout Mindset
books.author: Julia Galef
books.core_idea_en: Soldier mindset defends beliefs; scout mindset wants an accurate map. Tests: calibration, the double standard test, the outsider test, the selective sceptic test.
books.core_idea_ar: عقلية الجندي تدافع عن معتقداتها، وعقلية الكشاف تريد خريطة دقيقة؛ مع اختبارات المعايير المزدوجة والغريب والمتشكك الانتقائي.

books.title: Think Again
books.author: Adam Grant
books.core_idea_en: Think like a scientist (not preacher, prosecutor or politician): hold views as hypotheses, seek disconfirmation, and use a challenge network.
books.core_idea_ar: فكّر كعالِم لا كواعظ أو مدّعٍ أو سياسي: اعتبر آراءك فرضيات، ابحث عما ينقضها، واستعن بشبكة تتحداك.

books.title: The Demon-Haunted World
books.author: Carl Sagan
books.core_idea_en: The 'baloney detection kit': independent confirmation, debate, no arguments from authority, multiple hypotheses, quantify, every link must work, Occam's razor, falsifiability.
books.core_idea_ar: عدة كشف الهراء: تأكيد مستقل، نقاش، لا حجة بالسلطة، فرضيات متعددة، قِس، كل حلقة يجب أن تعمل، شفرة أوكام، قابلية التكذيب.

books.title: Algorithms to Live By
books.author: Brian Christian & Tom Griffiths
books.core_idea_en: Computer-science results for everyday choices: optimal stopping (37% rule), explore/exploit, sorting and caching, scheduling, overfitting, relaxation and randomness.
books.core_idea_ar: نتائج علوم الحاسب للقرارات اليومية: التوقف الأمثل (قاعدة 37%)، الاستكشاف مقابل الاستغلال، الترتيب والتخزين، الجدولة، الإفراط في التوافق، التخفيف والعشوائية.

books.title: Range
books.author: David Epstein
books.core_idea_en: In wicked (messy, delayed-feedback) domains, breadth, analogical thinking and sampling beat early narrow specialisation; use distant analogies.
books.core_idea_ar: في المجالات الفوضوية بطيئة التغذية الراجعة، يتفوق الاتساع والتفكير بالتشبيه وتجريب مجالات متعددة على التخصص المبكر الضيق.

books.title: Deep Work
books.author: Cal Newport
books.core_idea_en: Value comes from distraction-free concentration on cognitively demanding tasks; schedule it, protect it, and shut down shallow work deliberately.
books.core_idea_ar: القيمة تأتي من التركيز الخالي من المشتتات على المهام الصعبة؛ جدوله واحمِه وأغلق العمل السطحي عمدًا.

books.title: Made to Stick
books.author: Chip & Dan Heath
books.core_idea_en: Sticky ideas are Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional and told as Stories (SUCCESs); beware the curse of knowledge.
books.core_idea_ar: الأفكار الملتصقة: بسيطة، غير متوقعة، ملموسة، موثوقة، عاطفية، في قصة؛ واحذر لعنة المعرفة.

books.title: The Checklist Manifesto
books.author: Atul Gawande
books.core_idea_en: Complex work fails on ignorance and ineptitude; short DO-CONFIRM or READ-DO checklists at pause points catch the killer items.
books.core_idea_ar: العمل المعقد يفشل بسبب الجهل أو التقصير؛ قوائم قصيرة عند نقاط التوقف تلتقط البنود القاتلة.

books.title: Al-Muqaddimah
books.author: Ibn Khaldun
books.core_idea_en: Reports must be checked not only by their chain of narrators but against the nature of things (what is possible in society and nature); history has causes and cycles.
books.core_idea_ar: الأخبار لا تُفحص بسندها فقط بل بمطابقتها لطبائع العمران والممكن؛ وللتاريخ أسباب ودورات.

books.title: Doubts concerning Ptolemy / Book of Optics
books.author: Ibn al-Haytham
books.core_idea_en: The seeker of truth does not trust the writings of predecessors because they are revered; he doubts, examines, and tests by experiment (i'tibar).
books.core_idea_ar: طالب الحق لا يثق بكتب السابقين لمجرد تقديرها، بل يشك ويفحص ويختبر بالاعتبار (التجربة).

books.title: Al-Munqidh min al-Dalal
books.author: Al-Ghazali
books.core_idea_en: A method of systematic doubt: test each source of knowledge (senses, reason, authority) for what can actually establish certainty.
books.core_idea_ar: منهج شك منظم: اختبر كل مصدر للمعرفة (الحواس، العقل، التقليد) لما يمكنه فعلًا أن يثبت اليقين.

methods.use_when: estimating time, cost, success odds or any number for a plan you are inside of
steps: Name the reference class: similar projects done by others.
Find the base rate in that class (median duration, typical overrun, share that succeeded).
Only then adjust for what is truly different here, and keep each adjustment small and stated.
methods.check: the estimate cites a base rate and lists each adjustment with its reason
methods.trap: planning fallacy: building the number from the inside story of this one plan

methods.name_en: WYSIATI check (what you see is all there is)
methods.name_ar: فحص «ما تراه هو كل ما هناك»
methods.use_when: a confident conclusion was reached quickly from little information
steps: Write the conclusion in one sentence.
List the information you did NOT have that could flip it.
Ask: how good would this story have to be if half the facts were different? Lower confidence accordingly.
methods.check: the missing-information list is non-empty and confidence is stated after it
methods.trap: a coherent story feels true; coherence is not evidence

methods.use_when: a number or judgement may have been pulled by the first figure seen or by a vivid recent case
steps: Note the first number you saw and every vivid example that came to mind.
Re-estimate from an independent source or a different starting point.
If the two estimates differ by more than your stated tolerance, report the range, not the anchor.
methods.check: two independently derived numbers are shown
methods.trap: adjusting insufficiently away from an anchor that has no evidential value

methods.use_when: choosing between candidates, designs, hires or proposals where gut feel dominates
steps: Pick 4-6 independent attributes before seeing the options in detail.
Score each attribute separately, one attribute at a time across all options.
Only after scoring, form a global intuition; if it disagrees with the scores, write why.
methods.check: attribute scores exist and were recorded before the overall verdict
methods.trap: halo effect: one strong attribute colouring every other score

methods.use_when: the same kind of judgement is made repeatedly (reviews, grading, pricing, QA scores)
steps: Give the same case to two independent judges (or judge it twice, later, blind).
Measure the spread of the answers.
If the spread is larger than the decision tolerance, add a rubric or anchors and repeat.
methods.check: a measured spread is reported, not assumed
methods.trap: assuming agreement because nobody compared

methods.use_when: a complex decision with several dimensions (a launch, an acquisition, a big design choice)
steps: Break the decision into independent assessments, each with a fact-based question.
Have each assessment made separately, ideally by different people or passes.
Combine at the end in a single meeting/pass; discuss only after independent ratings are in.
methods.check: each dimension has its own recorded rating before the combined decision
methods.trap: letting an early overall impression contaminate the sub-assessments

methods.use_when: an estimate matters and more than one estimate can be obtained
steps: Collect estimates independently (no discussion first).
Average them (or take the median when outliers exist).
Report the spread as uncertainty.
methods.check: the estimators did not see each other's numbers before answering
methods.trap: group discussion first, which correlates the errors

methods.use_when: about to deliver a recommendation, review or report
steps: Survivorship: am I only looking at winners?
Sunk cost: would I choose this if I were starting today?
Confirmation: what did I search for that could have proved me wrong?
Social proof / authority: is 'everyone uses it' or 'X said so' doing the work?
Story bias: would the claim survive without its narrative?
methods.check: each question has a one-line answer in the audit
methods.trap: reading the list without answering it

methods.use_when: writing an ad, a landing page, a pitch, a call to action or a caption
steps: For each of the six levers ask: do we have a TRUE fact that activates it (a real testimonial, a real deadline, a real credential)?
Use only levers backed by a true fact; drop the rest.
Write the claim and the fact that backs it side by side.
methods.check: every persuasion lever in the copy points to a verifiable fact
methods.trap: fake scarcity or invented social proof (deceptive, and refused by this skill)

methods.use_when: evaluating an offer, a vendor pitch or a source that wants a fast decision
steps: Mark each lever the message uses on you.
Strip the levers and restate the bare offer: price, terms, evidence.
Decide on the bare offer only.
methods.check: the decision note contains the stripped offer
methods.trap: deciding while the urgency is still active

methods.use_when: a question looks unanswerable or needs a number with no direct data
steps: Split the question into factors you can estimate separately.
Give each factor a range, not a point.
Multiply/add with the ranges (think.py fermi) and report the range.
methods.check: a factor tree with ranges exists
methods.trap: false precision: one number with no range

methods.name_en: Outside then inside, then update in small steps
methods.name_ar: خارجي ثم داخلي ثم تحديث بخطوات صغيرة
methods.use_when: giving a probability for a future event and new information keeps arriving
steps: Start from the base rate of the reference class.
Adjust for case specifics.
When news arrives, move the number by an amount proportional to how diagnostic the news is; avoid both freezing and lurching.
methods.check: the forecast history shows the starting base rate and each update with its reason
methods.trap: overreacting to vivid news or underreacting to strong evidence

methods.use_when: the same person or tool makes repeated predictions or estimates
steps: Record every forecast as a probability with a date and a resolution rule.
When it resolves, score it: (probability - outcome)^2.
Review the average score and calibration buckets every N forecasts.
methods.check: a ledger of resolved forecasts exists
methods.trap: remembering hits and forgetting misses

methods.use_when: a question where reasonable people or sources disagree
steps: Collect the strongest version of each competing view.
Note what each view sees that the others miss.
Form a combined judgement that weights each view by its track record and evidence.
methods.check: at least two opposing views are steel-manned in the notes
methods.trap: picking a side first and collecting support later

methods.use_when: reviewing a past decision after a good or bad outcome (post-mortem, retro)
steps: Separate: what did we know then, what did we decide, what happened.
Classify the outcome: skill, luck, or missing information we could have got cheaply.
Change the process only for the controllable parts.
methods.check: the review has the three columns and a luck/skill call
methods.trap: treating a bad outcome as proof of a bad decision

methods.use_when: stating a belief or claim as certain
steps: Ask: would I bet real money on this at even odds?
Restate the belief as a percentage.
Write what evidence would change it.
methods.check: the claim carries a percentage and a change-my-mind condition
methods.trap: binary certainty language for uncertain claims

methods.use_when: a decision likely to be hijacked by emotion or short-term temptation
steps: Ask how you will feel about each option in 10 minutes, 10 months, 10 years.
Pre-commit: write the rule now that your future self must follow (e.g. no publishing after midnight).
methods.check: a pre-commitment rule is written down
methods.trap: deciding at the emotional peak

methods.use_when: allocating time, money or effort under deep uncertainty
steps: Put most resources in something very safe that cannot ruin you.
Put a small, capped share in many cheap bets with large upside.
Avoid the fragile middle that looks moderate but hides tail risk.
methods.check: the worst case of the whole allocation is survivable
methods.trap: medium-risk options that hide a ruin scenario

methods.use_when: checking a plan, system or pipeline for hidden ways to break
steps: Ask what happens if each input doubles, halves or disappears.
List single points of failure and irreversible steps.
Improve first by removing (dependencies, steps, debt) before adding.
methods.check: a list of shocks and the system's response to each
methods.trap: adding features to fix fragility caused by too many features

methods.name_en: Skin in the game / silent evidence
methods.use_when: trusting advice, a case study or a success story
steps: Does the source bear the cost if wrong?
Where are the failures that used the same method (silent graveyard)?
Discount accordingly.
methods.check: the note names who bears the downside and the missing failures
methods.trap: learning only from survivors

methods.use_when: a single big number, a chart or a claim about trends
steps: Compare the number with a relevant total (per capita, per user, % of).
Look for the 80/20: which few items carry most of the total?
Check whether a straight-line extrapolation is justified or the curve bends.
methods.check: the claim states a denominator and a comparison
methods.trap: lonely numbers with no denominator

methods.use_when: deciding whether to research more before acting, or an 'unmeasurable' factor like brand value or quality
steps: Give a 90% confidence interval for each uncertain variable.
Ask which variable, if known exactly, would most likely change the decision.
Measure only that one, with the cheapest small sample (rule of five: 5 samples give ~94% chance the median lies between min and max).
methods.check: the research plan names the highest-value variable
methods.trap: measuring what is easy instead of what changes the decision

methods.use_when: any non-trivial technical or analytic problem (bug, algorithm, layout, calculation)
steps: Understand: what is the unknown, what is given, what are the conditions? Draw it.
Plan: have I seen a related problem? Can I solve a simpler or special case? Work backwards from the goal?
Carry out: check each step.
Look back: verify the result another way; can the method be reused?
methods.check: the 'look back' verification is recorded
methods.trap: jumping to the plan before the unknown is stated

methods.use_when: stuck on a problem with no obvious path
steps: Specialise: try the smallest concrete instance.
Generalise: is there a broader problem that is easier?
Work backwards: what would the step just before the goal look like?
methods.check: at least one auxiliary problem was tried
methods.trap: staring at the full problem

methods.use_when: a first draft, design or solution is needed and perfectionism is blocking
steps: Produce a deliberately quick, imperfect attempt.
List exactly where and why it fails.
Each failure points at the next better attempt.
methods.check: a failure list drives version 2
methods.trap: polishing a first draft instead of learning from its failures

methods.use_when: learning a new tool, domain or codebase quickly
steps: Find the simplest core case and understand it completely.
Explain it without jargon.
Only then add the next layer.
methods.check: a plain-language explanation of the core exists
methods.trap: surface coverage of many features

methods.use_when: improving one property makes another worse (quality vs speed, size vs strength, detail vs file size)
steps: State the contradiction: improving X worsens Y.

Try principles: segmentation, taking out, local quality, asymmetry, merging, universality, nesting, prior action, dynamics, partial or excessive action, another dimension, feedback, self-service, copying, cheap short-living objects, inversion.
Prefer the idea that removes the contradiction over the one that compromises.
methods.check: at least three principles were tried and the chosen one removes rather than balances the conflict
methods.trap: settling for a midpoint compromise

methods.use_when: designing a solution from scratch or simplifying a heavy one
steps: Describe the result as if the function happened by itself with zero cost and no new parts.
Ask which existing resources (time, space, fields, waste) could do it.
Walk back from the ideal only as far as necessary.
methods.check: the solution reuses an existing resource
methods.trap: adding a new component for every function

methods.use_when: writing a report, recommendation, email, README or summary
steps: Situation: what the reader already accepts.
Complication: what changed.
Question: what the reader now asks.
Answer: the top line; then 2-4 supporting points, each MECE and each a summary of its own evidence.
methods.check: the first sentence is the answer and supporting points do not overlap
methods.trap: chronological storytelling of the work instead of the conclusion

methods.use_when: breaking a big question into parts (why are sales down, how to grow, what to build)
steps: Write the question at the top.
Split into branches that are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (e.g. price x volume).
Keep splitting until each leaf can be answered with one analysis.
methods.check: branches add up to the parent with no overlap
methods.trap: lists of causes that overlap and leave gaps

methods.use_when: an ambiguous business, product or research problem with limited time
steps: Define the problem precisely (who decides, criteria, timeframe, constraints).
Disaggregate with a logic tree.
Prioritise branches by impact x ability to influence; cut the rest.
Write a workplan with an early hypothesis per branch.
Analyse; synthesise into a so-what; communicate.
methods.check: the cut branches are listed with the reason they were cut
methods.trap: boiling the ocean: analysing every branch

methods.use_when: ideas keep coming out the same or the team is stuck
steps: Perceptual: are we seeing the problem too narrowly?
Emotional: fear of looking foolish, need for quick closure?
Cultural: 'that is not done here'?
Intellectual/expressive: wrong language (try sketch, numbers, story)?
Change the representation and regenerate.
methods.check: the named block and the changed representation are recorded
methods.trap: trying harder with the same representation

methods.use_when: evaluating an idea or plan with several viewpoints, or a council review
steps: Blue: define the focus and the sequence.
White: facts known and facts missing.
Green: alternatives and new ideas.
Yellow: benefits and why it could work.
Black: risks and why it could fail.
Red: gut feeling in one line, no justification.
Blue: summary and next step.
methods.check: each hat has its own output, black does not appear before yellow
methods.trap: mixing critique into idea generation

methods.use_when: need a non-obvious idea for a campaign, a product, a visual or a story
steps: Write a deliberately unreasonable statement (reverse, exaggerate, distort, wishful): 'PO the ad has no product in it'.
Move from it: what principle, benefit or feature does it suggest?
Shape the movement into a workable idea.
methods.check: the final idea traces back to a provocation
methods.trap: judging the provocation as if it were the proposal

methods.use_when: a creative brief with time to research (ad concept, brand, film idea)
steps: Gather: specific material about product/audience and general material from unrelated fields.
Digest: write fragments on cards and look for relations.
Incubate: switch to another task.
Catch: note the idea when it appears.
Shape: test it against the brief and the critics.
methods.check: the idea combines one specific fact with one general/outside element
methods.trap: skipping the gathering stage

methods.use_when: improving an existing product, template, video, design or workflow
steps: Substitute a part, Combine with something, Adapt from elsewhere, Modify/magnify, Put to another use, Eliminate a part, Reverse/rearrange.
Generate at least one variant per letter.
Keep the two strongest for testing.
methods.check: seven variants exist before selection
methods.trap: stopping at the first letter that works

methods.use_when: designing an app, a page, a service or a product for real users
steps: Discover: observe or interview users; collect pains in their words.
Define: one 'How might we...' statement.
Develop: many concepts, then cheap prototypes.
Deliver: test with users, keep what works, iterate.
methods.check: a 'How might we' statement and at least one user test exist
methods.trap: building the solution before defining the need

methods.use_when: an expensive build (render, app, animation) whose direction is not yet approved
steps: Make the lowest-fidelity version that answers the open question (storyboard, wireframe, 5-second preview).
Show it, collect reactions.
Spend on fidelity only after the direction passes.
methods.check: an approved low-fidelity artefact precedes the expensive build
methods.trap: rendering the final before the direction is agreed

methods.use_when: creating in the style of a reference or a trend
steps: Name 3+ influences, not one.
Extract the principle from each (rhythm, palette logic, framing), not the asset.
Combine the principles into something none of them made; credit the influences.
methods.check: no asset is copied and at least three influences are named
methods.trap: copying one source closely (and licence problems)

methods.use_when: a recurring problem that keeps coming back, growth that stalls, or side effects
steps: Name the stocks (what accumulates).
Name inflows and outflows.
Draw reinforcing and balancing loops and mark delays.
Ask which loop dominates now and which will dominate later.
methods.check: a loop diagram with at least one balancing loop and one delay
methods.trap: treating a symptom (a flow) instead of the structure

methods.use_when: choosing where to intervene in a system (team, product, process, audience)
steps: List candidate interventions.
Rank: numbers/parameters < buffers < structure < delays < feedback strength < information flows < rules < self-organisation < goals < paradigm.
Prefer the highest feasible rung.
methods.check: the chosen intervention's rung is stated
methods.trap: tuning parameters when a rule or information flow is the real lever

methods.use_when: a 'fix' that worked briefly and then made things worse
steps: Compare with archetypes: fixes that fail, shifting the burden, limits to growth, tragedy of the commons, escalation, success to the successful.
Name the match and its standard leverage (e.g. shifting the burden -> strengthen the fundamental solution).
methods.check: an archetype is named with its leverage
methods.trap: repeating the quick fix

methods.use_when: a marketing plan, business plan, channel strategy or growth plan
steps: Diagnosis: what is the critical obstacle (one paragraph)?
Guiding policy: the approach chosen to overcome it, and what it rules out.
Coherent actions: 3-5 actions that reinforce each other.
methods.check: the plan names what it will NOT do
methods.trap: a list of goals and buzzwords with no diagnosis

methods.use_when: before starting an important plan, render, release or launch
steps: Imagine it is six months later and the project failed badly.
Write every reason why it failed (each reviewer independently).
Turn the top reasons into checks or plan changes now.
methods.check: plan changes trace back to pre-mortem reasons
methods.trap: a generic risk list not tied to this plan

methods.name_en: Mental simulation of the chosen option
methods.use_when: an option was picked quickly by intuition
steps: Walk through the option step by step in its real context.
Note where the simulation snags (a step you cannot picture working).
Fix the snag or switch options.
methods.check: snags are listed
methods.trap: accepting an intuitive choice without simulating it

methods.use_when: competing for attention or market share against stronger players
steps: Map own strengths and limits honestly.
Map competitors' strengths and where they cannot follow (cost structure, brand, speed).
Choose the ground where your strength meets their weakness; avoid head-on fights.
methods.check: the chosen position names a competitor constraint
methods.trap: copying the leader on the leader's own ground

methods.use_when: a whether-or-not decision ('should I X?') or a narrow choice
steps: Widen: turn 'whether or not' into at least 3 options; ask 'what if this option vanished?'.
Reality-test: what would have to be true? run a small experiment (ooch).
Attain distance: what would I advise a friend? 10/10/10.
Prepare to be wrong: set a tripwire (a date or metric that triggers a rethink).
methods.check: 3+ options and a tripwire are written
methods.trap: narrow framing: a yes/no on a single option

methods.use_when: launching a product, feature, channel or content series
steps: List assumptions that must be true for success.
Pick the riskiest (most uncertain x most fatal).
Design the smallest experiment with a pass/fail metric set in advance.
Decide pivot or persevere on the result.
methods.check: the pass/fail threshold was written before the experiment
methods.trap: vanity metrics chosen after the fact

methods.use_when: a goal that is hard to reach directly (make it viral, make users stay, make the film great)
steps: Ask the inverse: how would we guarantee failure?
List the failure causes.
Remove or guard against each; what remains is the plan.
methods.check: a failure list was converted into guards
methods.trap: only brainstorming forward

methods.use_when: a change with obvious first effects (a price change, a new rule, a UI change, automation)
steps: Write the first-order effect.
Ask 'and then what?' twice for each affected group.
Check whether a second-order effect cancels the first.
methods.check: two levels of 'and then what' exist per group
methods.trap: stopping at the intended effect

methods.use_when: deciding whether to rely on own judgement or get an expert/tool
steps: Mark what you know well, partly, and not at all for this task.
Inside: act. Edge: verify. Outside: get an expert, a source or a tool, and say so.
methods.check: claims outside the circle carry a source or a caveat
methods.trap: confidence spilling outside the circle

methods.name_en: Bias tests (double standard, outsider, conformity, status quo)
methods.name_ar: اختبارات التحيز: المعيار المزدوج، الغريب، المسايرة، الوضع القائم
methods.use_when: evaluating own work, a favoured idea, or evidence that agrees with you
steps: Double standard: would I accept this evidence if it supported the other side?
Outsider: what would someone new to the situation conclude?
Conformity: would I hold this view if my peers didn't?
Status quo: if the current state were the proposal, would I choose it?
methods.check: each test has a one-line answer
methods.trap: motivated reasoning dressed as analysis

methods.use_when: revisiting a plan, design or belief that has been in place for a while
steps: State the belief as a hypothesis.
Write what result would falsify it.
Look for that result (data, user feedback, a challenge-network critic).
Keep, revise or drop; log the change.
methods.check: a falsification condition and its check are recorded
methods.trap: preacher mode: defending instead of testing

methods.use_when: checking a claim from the web, a tool's marketing, a viral post or a research summary
steps: Is there independent confirmation of the facts?
Are there competing hypotheses, and were they tested?
Is it quantified and falsifiable?
Does every link in the chain hold, not just most?
Is authority the only support?
methods.check: each claim in the deliverable has a source or is marked unverified
methods.trap: accepting a claim because it fits the narrative

methods.use_when: choosing between a known-good option and trying new ones (tools, styles, suppliers, content formats)
steps: Estimate the remaining horizon (how many more uses).
Long horizon: explore more; short horizon: exploit the best known.
Set an explicit exploration share (e.g. 20% of runs try something new) and review results.
methods.check: an exploration share and a review point are set
methods.trap: never exploring (stagnation) or always exploring (no compounding)

methods.use_when: sequential choices where you cannot go back (candidates, offers, locations, takes)
steps: Estimate the total number of options you can see.
Look at the first ~37% without committing, noting the best.
Then take the first option better than that benchmark.
methods.check: the benchmark set in the look phase is written
methods.trap: committing to the first decent option or searching forever

methods.use_when: a model, rule, metric or creative formula tuned on few examples
steps: Hold out examples not used for tuning.
Prefer the simpler rule unless the complex one wins on held-out cases.
Watch for optimising the metric instead of the goal (Goodhart).
methods.check: a held-out check exists
methods.trap: a perfect fit on the training cases

methods.use_when: a novel problem with no established playbook
steps: List 3-5 analogies from distant fields (biology, sports, cooking, architecture...).
For each, extract the structural mechanism.
Test which mechanism transfers.
methods.check: at least one analogy is from a distant field
methods.trap: using only the closest, most obvious analogy

methods.use_when: a long, demanding task (a full film edit, a refactor, a research report)
steps: Define the single outcome of the block.
Batch all shallow items (messages, checks) outside the block.
End with a shutdown note: what is done, what is next, where to resume.
methods.check: a resume note exists at the end of each block
methods.trap: interleaving many small checks inside the deep task

methods.use_when: a hook, script, slogan, explainer video or presentation
steps: Simple: the core message in one sentence.
Unexpected: what breaks the audience's guess?
Concrete: one sensory example.
Credible: a detail they can verify.
Emotional: why should this person care?
Story: a character, a problem, a turn.
methods.check: the script scores yes on at least 4 of 6
methods.trap: the curse of knowledge: abstract language the audience cannot picture

methods.use_when: a repeated, high-stakes procedure (export, release, render, publish, payment)
steps: Pick the pause points (before start, before irreversible step, before delivery).
Write 5-9 killer items per point that experts still forget.
Run it as DO-CONFIRM: do the work, then confirm each item aloud/in the log.
methods.check: the checklist is short, item-specific and its run is logged
methods.trap: long, generic checklists nobody reads

methods.name_en: Plausibility against the nature of things
methods.use_when: a surprising report, statistic or story, especially from a single source
steps: Check the source chain (who saw it, who passed it on).
Independently, check possibility: does it fit known constraints (physics, economics, base rates, logistics)?
If it is impossible or extreme, require stronger evidence before using it.
methods.check: both the chain and the plausibility check are noted
methods.trap: trusting a reliable-sounding source for an implausible claim

methods.name_en: Doubt the authority, test by experiment
methods.use_when: a tutorial, doc, popular repo or earlier session says something works
steps: Restate the claim as a testable statement.
Design the smallest experiment that would show it false.
Run it here and record the observed result, not the documented one.
methods.check: a local run result is recorded next to the claim
methods.trap: reporting documented behaviour as observed behaviour

methods.use_when: a deliverable mixes observed results, inferences and things taken on trust
steps: Tag each claim: observed (I ran/saw it), inferred (reasoned), or received (someone said).
Raise or lower confidence by tag.
State received claims as such in the deliverable.
methods.check: every key claim carries an observed/inferred/received tag
methods.trap: presenting received claims as observed
